sky.clear: Sky cover at one point of the session's weather timeline (Conditions panel): no clouds.
sky.overcast: Sky cover at one point of the weather timeline: the whole sky grey with cloud.
weather.nodeStart: Weather timeline: the first point, at the start of the session. The other points are 25%, 50%, 75% of the session.
weather.nodeFinish: Weather timeline: the last point, at the end of the session.
weather.overcast: Weather choice: dry, with a grey sky.
weather.lightRainDetail: Intermediates = the tyres for a damp track, between slicks and full wets.
weather.heavyRainDetail: Full wets = the tyres for heavy rain.
weather.drying: Weather choice: the rain has stopped and the track is drying.
weather.dryingDetail: A dry line = the racing line dries first while the rest of the track is still wet.
weather.dynamic: Weather choice: the weather changes during the session.
timeOfDay.goldenHour: Time of day: the hour before sunset, low warm sun.
raceStart.assisted: Race launch choice: the game holds the car until the start lights go out.
raceStart.manual: Race launch choice: the player works the clutch and revs at the start.
raceStart.manualHint: Jump penalty = time added for leaving before the lights go out. 's' = seconds.
realism.casual: Simulation realism level: the most forgiving.
realism.standard: Simulation realism level: the middle one.
realism.full: Simulation realism level: the complete model.
raceRules.auto: Race rules choice: picked from the car's class.
raceRules.endurance: Race rules for sports cars and GT cars.
raceRules.openWheelHint: Strikes = times the player left the track. +5 s = five seconds added to the race time.
raceRules.enduranceHint: Weighted points: bigger excursions off the track count for more. +5 s = five seconds added to the race time.
raceRules.trackLimitsOn: Track-limits rule switch in race setup: enforced.
raceRules.trackLimitsOff: Track-limits rule switch in race setup: not enforced.
raceSetup.gridBack: Where the player starts on the grid: at the back.
raceSetup.gridMiddle: Where the player starts on the grid: in the middle.
raceSetup.gridPole: Where the player starts on the grid: first place (pole position).
raceSetup.gridRandom: Where the player starts on the grid: a random place.
raceSetup.aiGridPace: How the AI cars are ordered on the grid: by their speed.
raceSetup.aiGridQualifying: How the AI cars are ordered on the grid: by a qualifying session.
raceSetup.aiGridReversed: How the AI cars are ordered on the grid: fastest at the back.
raceSetup.startAuto: Race start type choice: picked from the car's class.
raceSetup.startStanding: Race start type: cars start from a standstill on the grid.
raceSetup.startRolling: Race start type: cars start while already moving behind a pace lap.
raceSetup.standingStart: Lower case, at the end of a summary line after ' · ', e.g. '5 AI · 5 laps · Pro · standing start'.
raceSetup.rollingStart: Lower case, at the end of a summary line after ' · ', e.g. '5 AI · 5 laps · Pro · rolling start'.
raceSetup.aggressionClean: How the AI cars race: leave more room, pass less.
raceSetup.aggressionNormal: How the AI cars race: the default.
raceSetup.aggressionHard: How the AI cars race: brake later, defend more.
grip.green: Track grip choice: a clean track with almost no rubber on it.
grip.light: Track grip choice: a little rubber on the racing line.
grip.medium: Track grip choice: some rubber on the racing line.
grip.natural: Track grip choice: the usual rubber of a race weekend.
grip.heavy: Track grip choice: a lot of rubber on the racing line.
grip.saturated: Track grip choice: the most rubber the line can hold.
aiSkill.rookie: AI driver skill level, the lowest.
aiSkill.alien: AI driver skill level, the highest (gamer slang for an unbeatably fast driver).
challenge.conditions: The weekly challenge's rules in one line. {tyres}: the tyres every lap is driven on, already translated (e.g. 'Soft tyres'). Low fuel = the car carries little fuel.
challenge.tyresVintageSlicks: Slick racing tyres of an old (1970s–80s) design.
challenge.timeLeftDays: Time left in the weekly challenge, e.g. '3 d 4 h'. d = days, h = hours; use your language's short unit forms. The screen adds 'left' after it.
challenge.timeLeftHours: Time left, e.g. '5 h 12 min'. h = hours, min = minutes.
board.conditions: What a lap on the board was driven with, e.g. 'No assists · Full · Dry'. Each part is already translated.
board.assistsPro: Assist level of a lap: no driving aids.
board.assistsSemiPro: Assist level of a lap: a few driving aids.
board.assistsAssisted: Assist level of a lap: most driving aids on.
board.realismCasual: Simulation realism of a lap: the most forgiving.
board.realismStandard: Simulation realism of a lap: the middle level.
board.realismFull: Simulation realism of a lap: the complete model.
board.surfaceDry: Track surface of a lap: dry.
board.surfaceWet: Track surface of a lap: wet.
badges.weeklyGold: Badge name: first place in a weekly time-trial challenge.
badges.weeklySilver: Badge name: second place in a weekly challenge.
badges.weeklyBronze: Badge name: third place in a weekly challenge.
badges.fastestLap: Badge name: holds the fastest lap on a lap board.
badges.og: Badge name for early players (drove the first version of the physics). OG = 'original', slang; keep it if your players would know it.
badges.bulb: Badge name: gave the developer an idea or a contribution.
badges.times: A badge won several times, e.g. 'Weekly Gold ×2'. {badge}: badge name, already translated.
badges.withNote: A badge with the developer's note, e.g. 'Idea Contributor — Wet weather tyres'. {note}: written by the developer, not translated.
badges.medalDetail: Badge tooltip. {place}: first, second or third.
badges.medalDetailWeeks: Badge tooltip. {place}: first, second or third. {weeks}: the weeks it was won, e.g. '2026-W47 V2, 2026-W48 V2'; V2 = physics version.
badges.recordDetailCount: Fastest Lap badge tooltip. A board = a lap time board for one circuit and car; open = still taking laps.
badges.recordCar: One part of the Fastest Lap tooltip: a car and on how many boards it holds the record. {car}: car name, not translated.
badges.recordManual: Part of the Fastest Lap tooltip: records given by hand rather than counted by the game.
badges.recordDetail: Fastest Lap tooltip. {boards}: the parts above joined with ' · '. Tapping the badge lists the circuits.
badges.ogDetail: OG Driver badge tooltip. Physics V1 = the first version of the game's physics.
badges.bulbDetailNote: Idea Contributor badge tooltip. {note}: the developer's note, not translated.
badges.bulbDetail: Idea Contributor badge tooltip with no note.
challenge.placeNoTime: The player's place on this week's challenge board: no lap yet.
challenge.placeFirst: The player's place on this week's challenge board: first. P1 = position 1.
challenge.place: The player's place on the challenge board, e.g. 'P7'. P = position, as in racing.
challenge.placeGap: e.g. 'P7 · 0.214 to P6'. {gap}: seconds behind the place above, already formatted. {above}: that place's number.
camera.chaseClose: Camera view name: following close behind the car.
camera.chase: Camera view name: following behind the car.
camera.chaseFar: Camera view name: following further behind the car.
camera.chaseLow: Camera view name: following low behind the car.
camera.tvPod: Camera view name: the camera on top of the car above the driver's helmet, as on TV ('T-cam' in Formula 1).
camera.cockpitShoulder: Camera view name: from beside the driver's shoulder, inside the car.
camera.cockpit: Camera view name: from the driver's eyes.
camera.dash: Camera view name: from the dashboard, just ahead of the steering wheel.
camera.nose: Camera view name: from the front (nose) of the car.
camera.helicopter: Camera view name: from high above the car.
camera.tvSide: Camera view name: fixed TV cameras beside the track.
camera.free: Camera view name: a camera the player flies around freely.
music.poolMenu: A group of music tracks: the ones played in the menus. Settings > Audio shows it as the title of a list, followed by 'tracks'.
music.poolRace: A group of music tracks: the ones played during a race.
music.poolResults: A group of music tracks: the ones played on the results screen and in replays.
carQuality.ownBadge: Small badge on a car card, written in capitals: the car has physics made for it.
carQuality.own: Car browser filter: cars with physics made for them.
carQuality.sharedBadge: Small badge on a car card, in capitals: the car uses another car's physics.
carQuality.shared: Car browser filter: cars that use another car's physics.
carQuality.eraBadge: Small badge on a car card, in capitals: an older car driving on the 2026 physics.
carQuality.era: Car browser filter: older cars driving on the 2026 physics.
carClass.f1: Car class name: formula cars (single-seaters with open wheels).
carClass.f1Detail: Under the class name. DRS and active aero are moving wing systems; keep DRS as is.
carClass.gt3Detail: Under the GT3 class name. ABS = anti-lock brakes, TC = traction control; keep the abbreviations.
carClass.proto: Car class name: sports prototypes (closed-cockpit endurance race cars).
carClass.protoDetail: Under the class name. TC = traction control.
carClass.classic: Car class name: old sports and touring race cars.
carClass.classicDetail: Under the class name. Group 4, Group A and JGTC are racing categories; keep them as they are.
carClass.road: Car class name: cars made for public roads.
circuitQuality.originalBadge: Small badge on a circuit card, in capitals: a circuit made for LibreCorsa itself.
circuitQuality.original: Circuit browser filter: circuits made for LibreCorsa. LibreCorsa is the game's name.
circuitQuality.simBadge: Small badge on a circuit card, in capitals: a circuit built by hand for racing simulators.
circuitQuality.sim: Circuit browser filter: circuits built by hand for racing simulators.
circuitQuality.scanBadge: Small badge on a circuit card, in capitals: a circuit converted from a 3D scan.
circuitQuality.scan: Circuit browser filter: circuits converted from 3D scans.
circuitType.permanent: Kind of circuit: a purpose-built race track.
circuitType.street: Kind of circuit: on closed public streets.
circuitType.oval: Kind of circuit: an oval track.
circuitType.hillclimb: Kind of circuit: a road up a hill, driven as one timed run from start to finish.
livery.grid2026: Group of car paint schemes styled after the 2026 Formula 1 grid.
livery.retro: Group of car paint schemes in old (vintage) racing styles.
livery.colourChalk: Name of a paint colour swatch for the custom livery (read by screen readers).
livery.colourCarbon: Name of a paint colour swatch for the custom livery (read by screen readers).
livery.colourAlloy: Name of a paint colour swatch for the custom livery (read by screen readers).
livery.colourVermilion: Name of a paint colour swatch for the custom livery (read by screen readers).
livery.colourPapaya: Name of a paint colour swatch for the custom livery (read by screen readers).
livery.colourGold: Name of a paint colour swatch for the custom livery (read by screen readers).
livery.colourVolt: Name of a paint colour swatch for the custom livery (read by screen readers).
livery.colourEmerald: Name of a paint colour swatch for the custom livery (read by screen readers).
livery.colourCyan: Name of a paint colour swatch for the custom livery (read by screen readers).
livery.colourCobalt: Name of a paint colour swatch for the custom livery (read by screen readers).
livery.colourIndigo: Name of a paint colour swatch for the custom livery (read by screen readers).
livery.colourMagenta: Name of a paint colour swatch for the custom livery (read by screen readers).
keyActions.aero: A keyboard key action: switches the car's moving wings between X mode (low drag) and Z mode (high downforce). Keep X and Z.
keyActions.camera: A keyboard key action: press to change the camera view; hold to adjust the seat and camera.
keyActions.flyingLap: A keyboard key action: starts the lap again with the car already at speed.
keyActions.tvCamera: A keyboard key action: the fixed TV cameras beside the track.
keyActions.racingLine: A keyboard key action: show or hide the drawn ideal line on the road.
keyActions.mfdPage: A keyboard key action. MFD = multi-function display, the car's settings screen in the HUD; keep MFD.
keyActions.board: A keyboard key action: the lap time board shown while driving.
keyActions.neutral: A keyboard key action: put the gearbox in neutral.
keyActions.restart: A keyboard key action: restart the session.
padActions.aero: A controller button action: switches the car's moving wings between X mode (low drag) and Z mode (high downforce). Keep X and Z.
padActions.camera: A controller button action: press to change the camera view; hold to adjust the seat and camera.
padActions.flyingLap: A controller button action: starts the lap again with the car already at speed.
padActions.tvCamera: A controller button action: the fixed TV cameras beside the track.
padActions.racingLine: A controller button action: show or hide the drawn ideal line on the road.
padActions.mfdPage: A controller button action. MFD = multi-function display, the car's settings screen in the HUD; keep MFD.
padActions.board: A controller button action: the lap time board shown while driving.
padActions.neutral: A controller button action: put the gearbox in neutral.
padActions.restart: A controller button action: restart the session.
keyActions.boostHold: Keyboard action: the electric boost works while the key is held.
keyActions.boostLatch: Keyboard action: one press turns the electric boost on, the next turns it off.
keyActions.autopilot: Keyboard action: the computer drives the player's car.
keyActions.mouseSteer: Keyboard action: switch steering with the mouse on or off.
keyActions.throttleHalf: Keyboard action: half throttle while the key is held.
keyActions.replay: Keyboard action: watch the last seconds again.
padActions.boost: Controller button action: the electric boost.
padActions.headlights: Controller button action: a short press flashes the headlights, a long press switches them on or off.
pedals.notSet: A pedal with no control assigned. Lower case: shown inside a sentence.
pedals.trigger: Where a pedal is read: the controller's trigger (RT/LT). Lower case: shown inside a sentence.
pedals.stick: Where a pedal is read: one stick pushed one way, e.g. 'right stick up'. Lower case. Keep the {side} and {way} choices.
pedals.pressThrottle: Prompt at the start: how to press the throttle when no control is set.
pedals.holdButton: Prompt: hold a controller button. {button}: the button's name, e.g. RT.
pedals.pushStick: Prompt: push a stick one way, e.g. 'Push the right stick up'. Keep the {side} and {way} choices.
pedals.clutchPedal: The control the start cue names as the clutch on a steering wheel set. Lower case: shown inside a sentence.
pedals.button: A controller button with no standard name. {number}: its number.
padLayouts.gt: Controller layout named after Gran Turismo's default buttons.
padLayouts.gtClassic: Controller layout after older Gran Turismo games: the right stick is the throttle and brake.
padLayouts.f1: Controller layout after the official Formula 1 games' buttons.
padLayouts.forza: Controller layout after Forza Motorsport's buttons. Keep Forza.
padLayouts.bumper: Controller layout: gear changes on the shoulder buttons (bumpers).
wheelSupport.tested: Wheel support level: the developer has driven this wheel.
wheelSupport.expected: Wheel support level: should work, not tried yet.
wheelSupport.unknown: Wheel support level: may not work.
wheelSupport.no: Wheel support level: does not work this way.
wheelSupport.moza: Wheel support table note. WebHID is the browser's way to talk to the wheel; keep the word.
wheelSupport.hidPid: Wheel support table note. Keep driver and product names (WebHID, HID PID, HID++, hid-lg4ff, G HUB, bridge = the separate force-feedback helper program) as they are.
wheelSupport.directDrive: Wheel support table note. Keep driver and product names (WebHID, HID PID, HID++, hid-lg4ff, G HUB, bridge = the separate force-feedback helper program) as they are.
wheelSupport.pxn: Wheel support table note. Keep driver and product names (WebHID, HID PID, HID++, hid-lg4ff, G HUB, bridge = the separate force-feedback helper program) as they are.
wheelSupport.logitechClassic: Wheel support table note. Keep driver and product names (WebHID, HID PID, HID++, hid-lg4ff, G HUB, bridge = the separate force-feedback helper program) as they are.
wheelSupport.logitechHidpp: Wheel support table note. Keep driver and product names (WebHID, HID PID, HID++, hid-lg4ff, G HUB, bridge = the separate force-feedback helper program) as they are.
wheelSupport.logitechBridgeOnly: Wheel support table note. Keep driver and product names (WebHID, HID PID, HID++, hid-lg4ff, G HUB, bridge = the separate force-feedback helper program) as they are.
wheelSupport.thrustmaster: Wheel support table note. Keep driver and product names (WebHID, HID PID, HID++, hid-lg4ff, G HUB, bridge = the separate force-feedback helper program) as they are.
wheelSupport.thrustmasterBridgeOnly: Wheel support table note. Keep driver and product names (WebHID, HID PID, HID++, hid-lg4ff, G HUB, bridge = the separate force-feedback helper program) as they are.
wheelSupport.fanatecCslElite: Wheel support table note. Keep driver and product names (WebHID, HID PID, HID++, hid-lg4ff, G HUB, bridge = the separate force-feedback helper program) as they are.
hudLayouts.broadcast: HUD layout name: looks like TV race graphics.
hudLayouts.broadcastDetail: Tower = the list of positions down the side of the screen, as on TV.
hudLayouts.dash: HUD layout name: a screen like the one on a race car's steering wheel.
hudLayouts.telemetry: HUD layout name: shows the most car data.
hudLayouts.classic: HUD layout name: the game's original layout.
hudLayouts.minimal: HUD layout name: shows the least.
hudLayouts.irdashiesDetail: Under a HUD layout's name (the name is not translated). Shift lights = the lights that tell you when to change gear.
hudLayouts.racevisionDetail: Under a HUD layout's name. Relative = the cars just ahead and behind on the road; input pill and graph = small displays of the pedals.
hudLayouts.h2hDetail: Under a HUD layout's name. Deltas = time differences.
hudLayouts.retroDetail: Under a HUD layout's name. Delta bar = a bar showing time gained or lost against your best lap.
hudLayouts.grandPrixDetail: Under a HUD layout's name. Race tower = the list of positions.
steeringAssist.selfSteerStrength: Steering assist slider (controller and keyboard): the assist steers the wheels along the car's path and against slides.
steeringAssist.dampingStrength: Steering assist slider. Yaw = the car turning about its vertical axis.
steeringAssist.speedSensitivity: Steering assist slider: the steering gets slower at high speed.
steeringAssist.slipLimitMargin: Steering assist slider: how close to the tyres' grip limit the assist steers.
steeringAssist.slipLimitMarginHint: Understeer = the front tyres lose grip first. Peak slip = the slip angle where a tyre grips most.
steeringAssist.maxSelfSteerAngleDeg: Steering assist slider: the most the assist turns the wheels by itself. Lock = steering angle.
steeringAssist.presetBalanced: Steering assist preset name: the default.
steeringAssist.presetStable: Steering assist preset name: holds the car steadier.
steeringAssist.presetLoose: Steering assist preset name: lets the car move around more.
steeringAssist.presetDrift: Steering assist preset name: for sliding the car sideways on purpose.
steeringAssist.presetCalm: Steering assist preset name: steadier steering at high speed.
steeringAssist.fullLock: The steering turned as far as it goes. Lower case: the end of the preset detail line.
steeringAssist.presetDetail: What a steering assist preset does, lower case, one line. Each {…} is a value such as '50 %'; {grip} is a number; {cap}: '25°' or 'full lock'.
support.donatePayPal: Button to a modder's PayPal donation page. Keep PayPal.
support.supportOn: Button to a modder's support page. {site}: Patreon, Ko-fi, Streamlabs… (not translated).
support.donateToVia: Screen-reader name of the donation button. {maker}: the modder's name. {site}: PayPal.
support.supportOnSite: Screen-reader name of the support button. {maker}: the modder's name. {site}: Patreon, Ko-fi…
support.donateTo: Donation button where several stand together. {maker}: the modder's name.
support.supportMaker: Support button where several stand together. {maker}: the modder's name.
setupGroups.aerodynamics: Garage setup page title (F1 cars): wings and aero settings.
setupGroups.aerodynamicsShort: Short form of the setup page title 'Aerodynamics' for a narrow tab. Keep it very short (an abbreviation with a full stop is fine).
setupGroups.transmissionShort: Short form of the setup page title 'Transmission' for a narrow tab. Keep it very short (an abbreviation with a full stop is fine).
setupGroups.suspensionGeometryShort: Short form of the setup page title 'Suspension geometry' for a narrow tab. Keep it very short (an abbreviation with a full stop is fine).
setupGroups.suspensionShort: Short form of the setup page title 'Suspension' for a narrow tab. Keep it very short (an abbreviation with a full stop is fine).
setupGroups.electronicsShort: Short form of the setup page title 'Electronics' for a narrow tab. Keep it very short (an abbreviation with a full stop is fine).
setupGroups.mechanicalGripShort: Short form of the setup page title 'Mechanical grip' for a narrow tab. Keep it very short (an abbreviation with a full stop is fine).
setupGroups.thirdElementsShort: Short form of the setup page title 'Third elements' for a narrow tab. Keep it very short (an abbreviation with a full stop is fine).
setupGroups.fuelShort: Short form of the setup page title 'Fuel' for a narrow tab. Keep it very short (an abbreviation with a full stop is fine).
setupGroups.dampersShort: Short form of the setup page title 'Dampers' for a narrow tab. Keep it very short (an abbreviation with a full stop is fine).
setupGroups.brakesShort: Short form of the setup page title 'Brakes' for a narrow tab. Keep it very short (an abbreviation with a full stop is fine).
setupGroups.tyresShort: Short form of the setup page title 'Tyres' for a narrow tab. Keep it very short (an abbreviation with a full stop is fine).
setupGroups.aeroShort: Short form of the setup page title 'Aero' for a narrow tab. Keep it very short (an abbreviation with a full stop is fine).
setupGroups.thirdElements: Garage setup page: the third (heave) springs and dampers that hold up the car's floor.
setupGroups.mechanicalGrip: Garage setup page (GT cars): springs, anti-roll bars, brakes and differential.
setupSheet.tcSlip: Garage setting: a traction control (TC) dial. Keep TC.
setupSheet.tc1: Garage setting: a traction control (TC) dial. Keep TC.
setupSheet.tcCut: Garage setting: a traction control (TC) dial. Keep TC.
setupSheet.tc2: Garage setting: a traction control (TC) dial. Keep TC.
setupSheet.tcSlipAngle: Garage setting: a traction control (TC) dial. Keep TC.
setupSheet.abs: Garage setting: the anti-lock brakes dial. Keep ABS.
setupSheet.engineMap: Garage setting: which engine power map the car runs.
setupSheet.motorDeployment: Garage setting (hybrid cars): how much power the electric motor adds.
setupSheet.regeneration: Garage setting (hybrid cars): how much braking energy the electric motor recovers.
setupSheet.diffOnThrottle: Garage setting: how much the differential locks while accelerating.
setupSheet.diffOffThrottle: Garage setting: how much the differential locks while not accelerating.
setupSheet.diffPreload: Garage setting: the differential's locking force at rest.
setupSheet.brakeMigration: Garage setting: the brake balance moves rearward as the brake pedal is released.
setupSheet.gearSet: Garage setting: which set of gear ratios the car runs.
setupSheet.radiatorOpening: Garage setting: how open the radiator is (more cooling, more drag).
setupSheet.detached: Value of the anti-roll bar setting: the bar is disconnected.
setupSheet.toeIn: Value of a toe setting: the wheels point inwards. {angle}: e.g. '0.12°'.
setupSheet.toeOut: Value of a toe setting: the wheels point outwards. {angle}: e.g. '0.12°'.
setupSheet.dialOff: Value of a TC or ABS dial set to 0, written in capitals as on the car's dial.
setupSheet.blanketsOn: Value of the Tyre blankets switch: on.
setupSheet.blanketsOff: Value of the Tyre blankets switch: off.
setupSheet.engineMapMax: An engine map step, '<number> · <name>'. Keep the number.
setupSheet.engineMapRace: An engine map step, '<number> · <name>'. Keep the number.
setupSheet.engineMapSmooth: An engine map step, '<number> · <name>'. Keep the number.
setupSheet.engineMapLean: An engine map step: a lean fuel mixture, less power. Keep the number.
setupSheet.engineMapSave: An engine map step: saves fuel. Keep the number.
setupSheet.tyreBlankets: Garage setting: electric blankets that warm the tyres before the car leaves the garage.
setupSheet.frontThirdPacker: Garage setting: a spacer that limits the travel of the front third (heave) spring.
setupSheet.frontCornerPackers: Garage setting: spacers that limit the suspension travel at the front corners.
setupSheet.frontWheelRate: Garage setting: the stiffness of the front springs at the wheel.
setupSheet.frontBumpStopRate: Garage setting: the stiffness of the front bump stops (rubber stops at the end of the suspension travel).
setupSheet.frontBump: Garage setting: the front dampers' resistance when the suspension compresses.
setupSheet.frontRebound: Garage setting: the front dampers' resistance when the suspension extends.
setupSheet.frontFastBump: Garage setting: the front dampers' resistance to fast compression (kerbs, bumps).
setupFx.frontWing.more: Each setupFx pair says what raising (more) or lowering (less) a garage setting does, in a few words. Shown at the two ends of the setting's slider.
setupFx.blankets.less: With the tyre blankets off: the tyres are cold when the car leaves the garage. Out-lap = the first lap, driven to warm up.
padFeel.smooth: Controller steering feel choice: slower steering.
padFeel.default: Controller steering feel choice: the standard one.
padFeel.sharp: Controller steering feel choice: quicker steering.
padFeel.sharpDetail: Turn-in = how quickly the car starts to turn into a corner.
tyres.street: The one tyre a road car runs: road tyres, not racing tyres. Shown where other cars offer a choice of compounds.
setupShare.aeroLow: Part of a shared car setup's one-line summary: the low-drag aero package.
setupShare.aeroBalanced: Part of a shared setup's summary: the middle aero package.
setupShare.aeroHigh: Part of a shared setup's summary: the high-downforce aero package.
setupShare.soft: Part of a shared setup's summary: the soft tyre compound.
setupShare.medium: Part of a shared setup's summary: the medium tyre compound.
setupShare.hard: Part of a shared setup's summary: the hard tyre compound.
setupShare.intermediate: Part of a shared setup's summary: intermediate tyres (for a damp track), short form.
setupShare.wet: Part of a shared setup's summary: full wet tyres.
setupShare.chassisChanges: Part of a shared setup's summary: how many chassis settings differ from the car's default.
setupShare.brakeBias: Part of a shared setup's summary. BB = brake bias (front share of braking). {bias}: e.g. '56.5'.
setupShare.baseline: Summary of a shared setup that changes nothing from the car's default.
setupShare.factoryLowDrag: Name of a factory car setup for circuits with long straights: less wing, less drag.
trackLimits.flashbackDeleted: Banner while driving: the player used Flashback (rewind), so the lap no longer counts. Keep 'Flashback' if your language uses the game's term.
trackLimits.courseCutDeleted: Banner: the player cut the course (left the circuit's road and rejoined further on), so the lap no longer counts.
trackLimits.penaltyOnceBack: Banner detail in a race: the penalty is set once the car is back on the track.
trackLimits.leftLapRoad: Banner detail: the car left the road the lap is driven on.
trackLimits.courseCutPenalty: Banner: a course cut costs a time penalty. {seconds}: e.g. '5.0'; s = seconds.
trackLimits.secondsGained: Banner detail: time gained by the cut. {seconds}: e.g. '1.3'.
trackLimits.wallDeleted: Banner: the car leaned on or rode along a wall, so the lap no longer counts.
trackLimits.rodeWallBeforeLine: Banner detail: the car rode along the wall just before the finish line.
trackLimits.limitsDeleted: Banner: the car went beyond the track limits (all four wheels off the track), so the lap no longer counts.
trackLimits.offBeforeLine: Banner detail: the car went off the track just before the finish line.
trackLimits.nextLapToo: Banner detail: the next lap no longer counts either.
trackLimits.positionHandedBack: Banner: the player gave back the place they gained by leaving the track.
trackLimits.advantageGivenBack: Banner: the player gave back the time they gained by leaving the track.
trackLimits.noFurtherAction: Race control decision: no penalty. A standard racing phrase.
trackLimits.trackLimits: Banner title: about the track limits rule (staying within the white lines).
trackLimits.noAdvantage: Banner detail: going off gained nothing, so no penalty.
trackLimits.timePenalty: Banner: seconds added to the race time. {seconds}: e.g. '5.0'.
trackLimits.limitsCutMetres: Banner detail. {metres}: how many metres of the track were cut.
trackLimits.limitsMajorCut: Banner detail: a big part of the track was cut.
trackLimits.why: Why the player got a track limits strike. Keep the {reason} choices. Illegal overtake = passed a car while off the track.
trackLimits.limitsWhy: Same reasons as above, lower case after 'Track limits · '.
trackLimits.warningCount: Banner: a track limits warning. {count}/{max}: e.g. '2/3', warnings so far out of those allowed.
trackLimits.points: Track limits points so far, e.g. '2.75 pts'. pts = points.
trackLimits.strikes: Track limits strikes so far, e.g. '3 strikes'.
trackLimits.disqualified: Banner: the player is disqualified from the race for track limits.
trackLimits.limitsPoints: Banner detail. {points}: e.g. '2.75 pts' or '3 strikes', already translated.
trackLimits.blackWhiteFlag: Banner: the black-and-white flag, the last warning before a penalty (a motor racing flag).
trackLimits.nextPenalty: Banner detail. {why}: the reason, already translated. {seconds}: the next penalty in seconds.
trackLimits.nextDisqualification: Banner detail. {why}: the reason, already translated. The next strike disqualifies the player.
trackLimits.warningDetail: Banner detail. {why}: the reason; {points}: e.g. '2.75 pts' or '3 strikes'. Both already translated.
flags.yellow: Race control message in an online race: a yellow flag (danger ahead, slow down, no overtaking).
flags.trackClear: Race control message: the danger has passed (green flag).
flags.carStopped: Why the yellow flag is out.
flags.incident: Why the yellow flag is out: something happened on the track ahead.
connection.idle: Multiplayer status before connecting. A room = a private online lobby; the code is the room's short code.
connection.openingRoom: Multiplayer status. {code}: the room's code, e.g. 'K7Q2'.
connection.roomOpen: Multiplayer status. {code}: the room's code. Keep the • separator.
connection.roomOpenElsewhere: {code}: the room's code. Join = the Join button's label.
connection.roomServerUnreachable: Advanced = the name of a section of the multiplayer panel. A manual connection = pasting connection codes by hand.
connection.raceClosed: A scheduled online race refused the player: it is about to start.
connection.raceTaken: The player is already in the race in another browser tab or window.
connection.connectedPlayers: Multiplayer status: how many other players are connected.
connection.peerFailed: Couldn't make a direct connection to another player.
connection.peerBlocked: A network (often a mobile or office network) blocks direct player-to-player connections.
connection.hostingTabs: Multiplayer status: a race between browser tabs on this computer.
connection.playerLeft: Manual connection: the other player left; an offer is the connection code the host makes.
connection.makingOffer: Manual connection: making the connection code (offer) to send to the other player.
connection.offerReady: Manual connection: offer and answer are connection codes the two players copy to each other.
connection.answerReady: Manual connection: the answer is the connection code the guest sends back to the host.
connection.answerAccepted: Manual connection status. Keep the • separator.
connection.inNextRace: Status: the player has joined the next scheduled online race.
connection.connected: Multiplayer status: connected to the other player.
downloads.windowsSummary: Download section of the home page. WebHID = the browser feature for wheels; DualSense = the PlayStation 5 controller. Keep both.
downloads.windowsInstallNote: SignPath Foundation = a code-signing service; SmartScreen = Windows' download warning. 'More info' and 'Run anyway' are Windows button labels: use the words Windows shows in your language.
downloads.windowsStatusLabel: Badge: the Windows app is not code-signed.
downloads.macosStatusLabel: Badge: the macOS app is not code-signed.
downloads.macosInstallNote: 'System Settings > Privacy & Security' and 'Applications' are macOS names: use the names macOS shows in your language. A terminal command follows.
downloads.linuxInstallNote: FUSE2 / libfuse2 are Linux package names. A terminal command follows.
downloads.androidSummary: Trusted Web Activity, Game Mode: Android feature names.
downloads.androidStatusLabel: Badge: the Android app is signed. APK = the Android app file.
downloads.macosArm64Label: Download button for Macs with Apple's own chips. Keep 'Apple Silicon' and '.dmg'.
downloads.macosX64Label: Download button for Macs with Intel chips.
loading.circuit: Loading screen: what is downloading now, the circuit's 3D model.
loading.car: Loading screen: the player's car model.
loading.opponents: Loading screen: the other cars' models.
loading.shaders: Loading screen: preparing the graphics (compiling shaders) before the drive.
connection.ready: Multiplayer status before connecting: other browser tabs on this computer connect by themselves; other devices need the room code.
session.wheelDisconnected: Pause menu notice when the steering wheel is unplugged during a drive.
session.jumpStart: Race control: the player moved before the start lights went out (a penalty reason).
session.bigJumpStart: Race control: the player moved well off their grid spot before the lights went out.
session.clutchGearUp: Start prompt: the control the player holds as the clutch at a race start: the controller's Gear up button (the action's name in the controls list).
session.clutchPaddle: Start prompt: the control the player holds as the clutch on a steering wheel: the upshift paddle behind the wheel. Lower case: inside a sentence.
driverKey.notAKeyFile: Importing a driver key: the chosen file is not one. A driver key is the file that proves a player's name on the online lap boards.
driverKey.blocked: Importing a driver key: the browser's settings stop the game saving it (e.g. private mode).
board.renameUnreachable: Changing the player's name on the online lap boards: no answer from the server.
board.renameFailed: Changing the name on the online boards failed. {status}: the HTTP error number, e.g. 500.
simulator.formulaTeamCars: Lap board car filter: the board shared by all the Formula 1 team cars, which drive on one physics model.
simulator.lapNoLongerSaved: Posting a saved best lap: a faster lap has replaced it in this browser.
simulator.nameNotChanged: Changing the driver name failed (no reason given by the server).
simulator.setupLoadFailed: Notice after trying another driver's car setup from the lap board. {driver}: the driver's name.
simulator.setupMissing: Notice: that driver's lap has no car setup saved with it. {driver}: the driver's name.
simulator.setupApplied: Notice: another driver's car setup is now on your car. {driver}: their name. {summary}: a short summary such as 'Low drag · Soft · 3 chassis changes', already translated.
simulator.keySaved: Notice after exporting the driver key file. Post = upload lap times under your name.
simulator.noKeyYet: Notice: there is no driver key to export yet; the first lap upload makes one.
simulator.keyImportedFor: Notice after importing a driver key file. {name}: the driver name the key was saved with.
simulator.launchWheel: Prompt on the grid with a steering wheel: press the throttle pedal to start.
simulator.launchWheelSeat: Prompt on the grid with a steering wheel; holding the camera button adjusts the seat position.
simulator.launchPad: Prompt on the grid with a controller. {press}: how to press the throttle, already translated, e.g. 'Hold RT' or 'Push the right stick up'.
simulator.launchPadSeat: Prompt on the grid with a controller. {press}: e.g. 'Hold RT'. {button}: the camera button's name, e.g. RB.
simulator.launchTouch: Prompt on the grid with the touch controls.
simulator.launchKey: Prompt on the grid with a keyboard. {key}: the throttle key, e.g. W. Esc is a key; Menu = it opens the menu.
simulator.noRacesOnHillClimb: Why a race can't start: a hill climb is driven one car at a time.
simulator.backToRaces: Button after a scheduled online race: back to the list of races.
telemetryHud.menu: Button on touch screens (no Esc key) that opens the pause menu.
telemetryHud.calibratePedals: Button while driving when the wheel's pedals look uncalibrated: opens the pedal setup.
telemetryHud.holdForLightsOut: Prompt on the grid before the start lights go out.
telemetryHud.mouseSteering: Shown while steering with the mouse. {key}: the key that turns it off.
telemetryHud.keyMenu: Key hint at the bottom of the HUD, next to the Esc key (or the controller's Menu button): opens the menu.
telemetryHud.keyCamera: Key hint: changes the camera view.
telemetryHud.keyLine: Key hint: shows or hides the racing line (the drawn ideal line).
telemetryHud.keyBoard: Key hint: opens the lap board.
telemetryHud.replay: Badge while an instant replay plays.
trackGate.safeStart: Notice at start-up after the graphics card stopped the game last time (a lost WebGL context): the game starts in a safer mode. GPU = graphics card.
trackGate.graphicsLow: Notice at start-up after the graphics card stopped the game last time: the graphics preset was set to Low (the preset's name in Settings).
trackGate.loadFailedStaying: Notice: the chosen circuit could not load, so the current one stays. {circuit}: circuit name, not translated.
trackGate.loadFailedDefault: Notice: the circuit could not load, so the default one loaded. {circuit}: circuit name, not translated.
minimap.map: Screen-reader name of the circuit map in the HUD.
minimap.mapAtTurn: Screen-reader name of the circuit map. {turn}: the corner number the car is at.
minimap.facts: Under the circuit's name on the map. {country}: not translated. {length}: e.g. '4.32'. {unit}: km or mi.
minimap.sector: Map legend: the circuit's three timing sectors, each in its colour. {sector}: 1, 2 or 3.
minimap.elevation: Label of the circuit's height profile (how far the road rises and falls).
minimap.altitude: Height above sea level, abbreviated. {height}: e.g. '412 m'.
minimap.grade: How steep the road is here, in capitals. {grade}: e.g. '+4.2'.
minimap.profileStart: Under the height profile of a hill climb: the height at the start. {height}: e.g. '+12 m'.
minimap.profileStartFinish: Under the height profile: the height at the start/finish line. S/F = start/finish, abbreviated. {height}: e.g. '+12 m'.
source.sourceOf: Screen-reader name of the small button that shows where a car's or circuit's 3D model comes from. {title}: the model's title, not translated.
source.source: Tooltip of that button: where the 3D model comes from.
source.reportIssue: Link in that panel: report a problem with the model (for example a licence problem).
playError.title: Heading of the error page when the game crashes while starting.
playError.body: WebGL = the browser's 3D graphics; keep the word. Hardware acceleration = the browser setting that lets it use the graphics card.
playError.detail: Screen-reader name of the box with the technical error message (in English).
dash.yellowFlag: Banner on the GT3 car's dashboard screen (drawn in capitals) while a yellow flag is out.
badges.creator: Badge name for the person who made LibreCorsa.
account.checking: Quiet line while the game asks the server about the player's account.
account.passkey: A passkey on its own, as on its button. A passkey is the standard password-free sign-in (WebAuthn).
account.aPasskey: A passkey inside a sentence and a list: “Signed in with Discord and a passkey”.
account.justNow: Fills {ago} in sentences like “Synced {ago}”: under a minute ago.
account.join.named: Question before this device joins an account. {name} is the account's driver name; {ways} is a list of sign-in names already joined in the player's language: “Discord”, “Discord and Google”, “Discord, Google and a passkey”.
account.join.namedOnly: Question before this device joins an account. {name} is the account's driver name.
account.join.this: Question before this device joins an account with no driver name yet. {ways} is a list of sign-in names already joined in the player's language: “Discord”, “Discord and Google”, “Discord, Google and a passkey”.
account.join.thisOnly: Question before this device joins an account with no driver name yet.
